title: Two-layer graded-free cover of an arbitrary right DG module, surjective on cocycles
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A=\bigoplus_{r\in\mathbf Z}A^r$ be an associative unital graded ring with additive differential $d_A:A^r\to A^{r+1}$, $d_A^2=0$, and $d_A(ab)=d_A(a)b+(-1)^ra\,d_A(b)$ for $a\in A^r$. A right DG $A$-module is a graded right module $N$ with additive differential $d_N:N^s\to N^{s+1}$, $d_N^2=0$, and $d_N(na)=d_N(n)a+(-1)^sn\,d_A(a)$ for $n\in N^s$; a DG map preserves degree, action and differential. The shift $A[k]$ has $A[k]^r=A^{r+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_A$ and unchanged right action. Suppose the underlying sets of $A,N$ lie in a Grothendieck universe $u$. There exist a right DG $A$-module $Q$, a DG map $\pi:Q\to N$, disjoint sets $U,V$ in $u$, integers $t_w$ for $w\in U\amalg V$, and a homogeneous graded right $A$-basis $(e_w)_{w\in U\amalg V}$ of $Q$, with $|e_w|=t_w$, such that $Q$ has underlying sets in $u$, $\pi:Q^r\to N^r$ and $\ker(d_Q:Q^r\to Q^{r+1})\to\ker(d_N:N^r\to N^{r+1})$ are surjective for every $r$, $d_Q(e_u)=0$ for $u\in U$, and $d_Q(e_v)\in\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ for $v\in V$. In particular $Q_U=\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ is a DG submodule, its inclusion into $Q$ has a graded right $A$-linear retraction, and $Q_U$ and $Q/Q_U$ are isomorphic as DG modules to $\bigoplus_{u\in U}A[-t_u]$ and $\bigoplus_{v\in V}A[-t_v]$, respectively. No boundedness, commutativity or countability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, statement and proof (the disks-and-cycles construction, with its homogeneous basis and universe bound made explicit).

proof.text: Put $E=\coprod_{k\in\mathbf Z}N^k$ and $Z=\{(k,z)\in E:d_Nz=0\}$. For each $(k,m)\in E$ introduce distinct symbols $x_{k,m},y_{k,m}$ of degrees $k,k+1$; for each $(k,z)\in Z$ introduce a symbol $s_{k,z}$ of degree $k$. Take $V$ to consist of the $x$ symbols and $U$ of the $y,s$ symbols, using disjoint tags, and write $t_w$ for the indicated degrees. Define $Q^n$ to be the additive group of finite-support families $(a_w)$ with $a_w\in A^{n-t_w}$. Write such a family as $\sum_we_wa_w$ and define $(e_wa)b=e_w(ab)$ for homogeneous coefficients, extending additively. Coordinatewise distributivity, associativity and the unit law follow from those of $A$. Thus $Q=\bigoplus_nQ^n$ is a graded right $A$-module with the displayed homogeneous graded basis.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text:
Write $\delta_{x_{k,m}}=e_{y_{k,m}}$ and $\delta_y=\delta_s=0$. Define an additive map on finite-support families by
$$D(e_wa)=\delta_wa+(-1)^{t_w}e_wd_Aa.$$
Unique coordinates and additivity of $d_A$ make this well-defined; only the finitely many input coordinates and their paired $y$ coordinates can occur in the output. Both terms have degree $t_w+|a|+1$. For homogeneous $a,b$, the algebra Leibniz identity gives
$$D(e_wab)=\delta_wab+(-1)^{t_w}e_wd_A(a)b+(-1)^{t_w+|a|}e_wa\,d_A(b)=D(e_wa)b+(-1)^{t_w+|a|}e_wa\,d_A(b).$$
Adding proves the module Leibniz identity for homogeneous finite sums. Also $d_A(1)=0$: applying the algebra Leibniz identity to $1\cdot1$ gives $d_A(1)=d_A(1)+d_A(1)$. Hence $D(e_w)=\delta_w$.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text:
For a $y$ or $s$ generator, $D^2(e_wa)=(-1)^{2t_w}e_wd_A^2a=0$. For $w=x_{k,m}$ the two mixed terms cancel:
$$D^2(e_wa)=(-1)^{k+1}e_{y_{k,m}}d_Aa+(-1)^ke_{y_{k,m}}d_Aa+e_wd_A^2a=0.$$
By additivity this holds on all finite sums, so $d_Q=D$ makes $Q$ a right DG module. In particular $d_Q(e_u)=0$ for $u\in U$, while $d_Q(e_{x_{k,m}})=e_{y_{k,m}}$ belongs to the $U$ coordinate submodule.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text:
Set $p_{x_{k,m}}=m$, $p_{y_{k,m}}=d_Nm$, and $p_{s_{k,z}}=z$, and define $\pi(\sum_we_wa_w)=\sum_wp_wa_w$. This is additive, degree-preserving and right $A$-linear by distributivity and associativity. For each symbol, $d_Np_w=\pi(\delta_w)$: this is the definition for $x$, the equation $d_N^2m=0$ for $y$, and the defining cocycle condition for $s$. Consequently
$$d_N(p_wa)=\pi(\delta_w)a+(-1)^{t_w}p_wd_Aa=\pi D(e_wa).$$
Adding proves that $\pi$ commutes with differentials. Every $m\in N^k$ has preimage $e_{x_{k,m}}\in Q^k$. Every $z\in\ker(d_N:N^k\to N^{k+1})$ has the cocycle preimage $e_{s_{k,z}}$. This proves both required surjections in every degree.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text: The coordinate submodule $Q_U=\bigoplus_{u\in U}e_uA$ is stable under $D$ because $D(e_ua)=(-1)^{t_u}e_ud_Aa$. The projection retaining the $U$ coordinates and killing the $V$ coordinates is graded right $A$-linear and retracts its inclusion. The map $Q\to\bigoplus_{v\in V}e_vA$ that retains the $V$ coordinates is surjective with kernel exactly $Q_U$, so on cosets it gives a bijective graded right $A$-linear coordinate identification of $Q/Q_U$. Its inverse sends a finite family of $V$ coordinates to its coset. Since $\delta_v\in Q_U$, the differential on the quotient satisfies $D(\bar e_va)=(-1)^{t_v}\bar e_vd_Aa$.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text: For a generator of degree $t$, the map $a\mapsto e_wa$ identifies $A[-t]^n=A^{n-t}$ with its coordinate in degree $n$. Its differential is $(-1)^{-t}d_A=(-1)^td_A$, exactly the differential computed above. Thus these coordinate maps, and their coefficient-reading inverses, give DG isomorphisms $\bigoplus_{u\in U}A[-t_u]\simeq Q_U$ and $\bigoplus_{v\in V}A[-t_v]\simeq Q/Q_U$. All maps preserve the unchanged right actions. The retraction in the previous step need only preserve the graded module structure.

source.place: Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, proof (disk generators and additional cocycle generators); definition-shift for the shift convention.

proof.text: All the sets constructed lie in $u$. The integers lie in the module universe, and the hypothesis places the homogeneous underlying sets of $A,N$ there. Closure of a Grothendieck universe under indexed unions and subsets puts $E,Z$ and their finitely tagged copies $U,V$ in $u$. Put $W=U\amalg V$. For each $n$, finite-support coefficient families form a subset of the function set from $W$ to the underlying set of $A$, with the degree constraints imposed; function sets are subsets of power sets of Cartesian products, hence belong to $u$. Therefore $Q^n\in u$ and $\coprod_nQ^n\in u$. The same argument applies to the finite-support total graded module. The construction indexed every homogeneous element and every cocycle, without any countability, boundedness or commutativity restriction.
